sections.h2: What a lady bird deed is
sections.html:
A lady bird deed, also called an enhanced life estate deed, leaves the owner a life estate with extra powers and names the people who take afterward. The Department of Revenue addressed its tax treatment in advisement TAA 20B4-004, dated October 16, 2020.

Start with the deed's own wording: which powers the owner keeps and who the named remainder people are. Two deeds that both get called lady bird deeds can read differently, and the recorded text controls. Read yours line by line before you plan a sale.

sections.h2: Documentary stamp tax on a lady bird deed
sections.html:
In that advisement the answer was no, on the facts presented. The department concluded the deed did not transfer any present beneficial interest, so it owed no documentary stamp tax regardless of consideration.

The facts mattered. The life tenants in that request kept full powers over the property, and a deed that gives up some of those powers could be analyzed differently. Check with the clerk of court or a Florida real estate attorney before you record, because the tax is paid at the clerk's office.

An ordinary life estate deed is on the department's taxable list. The reasoning that no present beneficial interest moves is what separates an enhanced life estate deed from it.

sections.h2: Selling a home held under a lady bird deed
sections.html:
A sale begins with a deed to the buyer signed with the formalities Florida requires, so the first question is who must sign.

Section 689.01 requires a land conveyance to be written and signed before two subscribing witnesses. No seal is needed, and the witnessing can be done by audio-video technology. Whether the named remainder people must also sign depends on the powers written into your deed. The title agent reads the recorded text before agreeing to insure, so raise the question with the agent before you list.

  • Pull the recorded deed from the clerk's official records.
  • Check which powers the deed reserves to the owner, including selling and mortgaging.
  • Find out whether the underwriter will insure with only the owner signing.
  • Expect the sale deed to be taxed at the standard doc stamp rate.

sections.h2: Effect on the property tax bill
sections.html:
The tax result turns on whether the transfer counts as a title change. Under section 193.155, a sale, foreclosure or other transfer of legal or beneficial title sends the assessment back to just value the next New Year's Day. Spousal transfers and certain transfers at death are among the exceptions.

The state's cap chart shows 2.7 percent for 2026, 2.9 percent for 2025 and 3.0 percent for 2024, a year when CPI ran 3.4 percent and the 3 percent ceiling governed. The advisement reasoned that nothing beneficial passes when the deed is signed. Ask the property appraiser whether the office reads your deed the same way before you rely on that.

The homestead exemption is worth up to $50,000. The first $25,000 reaches school taxes, and the second $25,000 applies to non-school taxes on value above $50,000. Form DR-501 starts it, and renting the unit or moving out ends it.

sections.h2: Carrying the tax cap to a replacement home
sections.html:
Portability lets an owner move part of the Save Our Homes savings to a new Florida home. The new homestead must be set up within three years counted from the opening day of the calendar year the old one was abandoned. The sale date plays no part in that count.

File Form DR-501T with the new DR-501 before the early-spring deadline. Section 193.155(8) reduces the new home's assessed value by the lesser of $500,000 or the gap between just value and assessed value on the old home. Amendments from chapter 2026-239 first apply to the 2027 tax roll, so ask the property appraiser which version covers your filing year.

  • The old home's sale resets the buyer's assessment to just value.
  • Filing for homestead closes on March 1.
  • Residence must be in place on the assessment date, January 1.
  • Renting the home, moving out or leaving Florida ends the exemption.

sections.h2: Deed types and doc stamp tax
sections.html:
Deed type drives the tax result, who must sign and what the title insurer will accept.

Deed typeDoc stamp result
Lady bird (enhanced life estate), on the facts in TAA 20B4-004Not subject, regardless of consideration
Life estate deedListed as a taxable deed
Quit claim deedListed as a taxable deed
Agreement or contract for deedListed as a taxable deed

Two rules apply to any taxable deed. Everyone named on the document is liable for the tax, and if one party is exempt a non-exempt party must pay. Deeds are taxable whether or not they are recorded. Recording costs follow section 28.24, which also adds a $1.00 charge for each name beyond four on an instrument.

sections.h2: Documents to line up before listing
sections.html:
Begin with the recorded deed and the questions it raises: who holds the life estate, which powers are reserved, and who is named to receive the property later. Take the answers to the title agent, then to the closing attorney if anything is unclear.

  • Government photo identification for each person who will sign the sale deed.
  • The names of two adults who can witness the signing in person or by audio-video link.
  • A payoff statement for any mortgage on the property.
  • Your latest tax bill, to see whether homestead is applied.

Each item shortens the gap between a signed contract and a recorded deed, and a seller who arrives with them gives the title company fewer reasons to pause.

sections.h2: Selling fast with a lady bird deed in place
sections.html:
Cash buyers still want clean title. Gather the recorded deed, the legal description and any mortgage payoff before you talk to them.

The closing agent verifies each signer, pays off liens from proceeds and sends the sale deed for recording with its tax. After an owner's death, the deed's own terms and any probate steps decide who signs next, and the underwriter will say which court papers it wants. Recording questions go to the clerk's office.

A cash sale skips a lender's appraisal and underwriting, so the title review of your deed is usually the longest step. Giving the agent the recorded deed on day one is the easiest way to shorten it.

faqs.q: Is a lady bird deed subject to Florida doc stamp tax?
faqs.a: Not on the facts in advisement TAA 20B4-004, dated October 16, 2020, where the life tenants kept full powers. The department found no present beneficial interest passed, so no tax applied regardless of consideration. Confirm your own facts with the clerk or an attorney.

faqs.q: Do I need two witnesses on a lady bird deed?
faqs.a: Yes. Section 689.01 calls for a written deed with two subscribing witnesses. A seal is optional, and audio-video witnessing is allowed.

faqs.q: May a life tenant list and sell the property?
faqs.a: Often yes, depending on the powers your deed reserves. Show the title company the recorded deed first. It will tell you whether your signature alone is enough or the named remainder people must join.

faqs.q: Does a lady bird deed keep my homestead exemption?
faqs.a: The exemption depends on the home staying your permanent residence, not on the deed type. Renting or moving out ends it, and a title change resets the Save Our Homes assessment. Ask the county property appraiser how your deed is classified.

faqs.q: Which office records a lady bird deed?
faqs.a: The circuit court clerk serving the land's county. Any documentary stamp tax is collected there at recording, along with the page fees in section 28.24.
